meta.title: garage-door-position-tracker-codex-handoff
meta.authoring_context: OpenAI ChatGPT handoff for continuation in Codex app
meta.summary: Handoff-Datei für die Weiterarbeit am Projekt zur Garagentor-Positionsbestimmung per NFC mit ESP. Enthält Bedarf, Konzept, Ist-Stand, technische Entscheidungen, bekannte Probleme, Lösungsansätze und nächste Schritte für Zigbee-fähige ESP-Hardware.

project.name: garage-door-position-tracker
project.goal: Nicht-invasive Überwachung eines Lamellentors/Garagentors mit diskreten NFC-Markern zur Ableitung von Öffnungsgrad und Bewegungsrichtung, später als Zigbee-Gerät integrierbar.
project.current_phase: NFC reader prototype on ESP32-C3 with BLE debug and Wi-Fi diagnostics; Zigbee integration planned next on Zigbee-capable ESP32

need.problem_statement: Das Garagentor soll zuverlässig überwacht werden, ohne Eingriff in den Antrieb oder dessen Steuerung. Für den sicherheitskritischen Zustand 'wirklich geschlossen' soll ein separater Homematic IP Sensor verwendet werden. Zusätzlich werden grobe bis mittlere Zwischenstände des Tors benötigt, um den Öffnungsgrad und die Bewegungsrichtung abzuleiten.
constraints: Keine Änderungen an der Torsteuerung oder am elektrischen Antrieb
Closed-Status muss separat und besonders zuverlässig abgesichert sein
NFC soll als markerbasierte Positionslogik dienen, nicht als sicherheitskritischer Endlagensensor
Entwicklung zuerst auf vorhandener Hardware testen, danach auf Zigbee-fähige Hardware migrieren
non_goals: Keine sicherheitskritische Freigabe ausschließlich über NFC
Keine hochpräzise kontinuierliche Messung in Prozent mit Sub-Prozent-Auflösung

concept.core_idea: Mehrere NFC-Tags werden in definierter Reihenfolge entlang der Torlamellen angebracht. Ein stationärer Reader liest die UID der vorbeifahrenden Tags. Die Reihenfolge der Tags entspricht der Position des Tors. Daraus werden Index, Öffnungsgrad und Bewegungsrichtung abgeleitet.
why_nfc: UID-only Ansatz ist robust und einfach
Mechanisch einfacher testbar als Wellenencoder in der frühen Phase

important_architecture_decision.safe_closed_state: separat über Homematic IP Kontakt / Sensor
important_architecture_decision.nfc_role: diskrete Positionsmarker für Öffnungsgrad und Richtung
important_architecture_decision.future_transport: Zigbee on a Zigbee-capable ESP32 in later phase

tag_strategy.principle: UID-only mapping; Tag content is irrelevant
tag_strategy.position_model: array order defines logical position index

current_prototype.wireless_debug: BLE UART-like debug output via NimBLE using Nordic UART Service UUIDs

next_target.mcu: ESP32 with Zigbee support (user now has the proper Zigbee-capable ESP32 module available)
next_target.intent: migrate prototype logic to Zigbee-capable hardware as next development step

other_systems.closed_status_sensor: Homematic IP sensor/contact planned for secure closed verification
integration_targets: FHEM / MQTT potentially later depending on final architecture

key_decisions.reason: best/schnellste Schnittstelle for this project; wiring complexity is acceptable
simpler and more robust than reading NDEF/text payload
0..100 integer is sufficient; simpler and better for embedded logic and later Zigbee/MQTT use
lighter and more suitable than the older BLE stack for ESP32-C3 prototype debugging

features: UID reading with low timeout / high read rate
suppression of repeated log spam for same UID
periodic Wi-Fi RSSI logging every 5 seconds
UID -> index lookup by array order
state stabilization with candidate/stable index logic
current_firmware_state.purpose: Prototype and debug the sensor concept independent of Zigbee.

observed_problem_and_solution.problem: At tag transition zones, especially between two neighboring tags, the reader alternates rapidly between both tags (e.g. index 0 and 1). Naive logic interpreted every single alternating read as a real direction change, causing false switching between 'oeffnet' and 'schliesst'.
observed_problem_and_solution.evidence_summary: Observed test sequence during opening: repeated 0 -> 1 -> 0 -> 1 oscillation within tens of milliseconds. This is physically implausible as actual repeated reverse motion and indicates reader overlap / transition bouncing.

solution.name: stableIndex + candidateIndex hysteresis / confirmation logic
details: Do not treat every single read as a confirmed new position
Only promote candidateIndex to stableIndex after repeated detection count and/or minimum time
Ignore single-step opposite-direction impulses when a direction is already active

reported_values: derived quality class: sehr gut / gut / kritisch / schlecht
wifi_diagnostics.purpose: Assess Wi-Fi reception quality in the garage during tests

ble_debug.pattern: Nordic UART Service compatible BLE log output

coding_style_preferences: prefer integer state over float when sufficient
keep logs informative but not spammy
important_runtime_behaviour: same UID should not repeatedly spam log while tag remains present
same tag may be logged again after it has left the field long enough
direction should only change after stable confirmation
Wi-Fi diagnostics should not block NFC reading loop

next_step_zigbee.goal: Port the validated NFC/index/direction logic from the ESP32-C3 prototype to the newly available Zigbee-capable ESP32 module.
next_step_zigbee.expected_transport_role: Expose opening percentage and direction to Zigbee2MQTT
recommended_approach: Keep NFC/logic and transport abstraction separated
Replace or supplement current BLE/Wi-Fi debug transport with Zigbee state publishing
Model the device either as a generic sensor/cover position reporter or another Zigbee representation depending on desired exposes in Zigbee2MQTT
Preserve separate secure closed-state handling through Homematic IP or another independent reliable sensor
open_questions_for_codex: Which exact Zigbee-capable ESP32 module is now available (e.g. ESP32-C6, H2-based board, or other)?
Which framework should be used for Zigbee implementation: Arduino core Zigbee support vs ESP-IDF?
How should the device be modeled in Zigbee2MQTT: cover-like percentage, generic numeric sensor, or custom converter/exposes?

codex_prompt_seed.intent: Continue this project in Codex. First preserve the validated prototype logic. Then prepare a Zigbee-capable implementation path using the newly available Zigbee-capable ESP32 board.
instructions: Do not redesign the concept from scratch unless a hard technical blocker exists
Treat the current ESP32-C3 implementation as validated prototype baseline
Preserve UID order as the source of index truth
Keep secure closed-state as a separate concern from NFC marker logic
When migrating to Zigbee, separate domain logic from transport/output layers

confidence.notes: High confidence for the documented prototype architecture and current solution path. Zigbee migration specifics depend on the exact newly available Zigbee-capable ESP32 board and chosen framework.
